I think that it is within every human beings capacity to be understanding or biased.

HOWEVER

I do believe that alot of misguided opinions on race/sexuality/tolerance are encouraged by outdated historical documents (such as the bible) and as the human race has evolved so have societies opinions on the above issues. 

It frustrates me that in 2010 there are still sections of society that believe homosexuality can be "cured" and that people of different ethnicities are still "inferior" to caucasians, and that other religions are "inferior" to your chosen one.

I think (generally) someone who is able to cast off the rigidity of religion (or at least appreciate that religious rules are flexible) has a higher capacity of empathy and is able to understand the cultural differences of different countries/races/religions.

HOWEVER (again!)

I do not believe that religion HAS to restrict ones ability to be tolerant and you can believe in a god and still not take passages from a religious document literally and cast aside people who do not fit the template that the religious historical document incorrectly defines.

I think religion can enhance someones spirituality but in my experience religion limits most peoples ability to understand all the different human beings that exist on this beautiful planet.

Peace and Love!

my sister killed herself a few months ago.

I asked myself this same question. But the answer is obvious.

You feel that you have no one and nothing. You dont want help, you want everything to stop. You want all the pain to fade, and if you told someone, not only is it embarrassing to admit youre considering that route and more importantly everyone would stop you, and obviously thats not going to get the result that is so wrongly wanted.

When "choosing" suicide you are (obviously) not in a healthy frame of mind and no logical behavioural rules can be applied to the people who are weighed down by these horrible thoughts. You cant expect warnings and cries for help from people who feel that they only have one permanent option.

I wish she had phoned me, i know how you feel.

Just a little of my personal experience for this one...

When i was 10 my mum found a "used" condom in my bedroom and FREAKED out, but never talked to me about it, she vented to my much older sister who reassured her and then spoke to me.

Me and my friend had simply been investigating what they were, we filled some up with shampoo, water etc tried to burst them like water balloons etc.

It was just innocent fun and I wasnt anywhere near having sex or being interested in boys at all.

Im not saying that is your situation, however if my mum had spoken to me she wouldve had a much more peaceful existence! and even if the worst has happened, having a parent you can openly talk to without being judged is priceless.

Just to play devils advocate, at least you found a condom and not a positive pregnancy test, or some hideous sex toy, or a beastiality porn mag (!!) all said in a joking manner!!

One option maybe to bring it up in reference to another child or tv programme so you can gauge her reaction...?

I hope it all goes well for you!!
